If you’ve received a late filing penalty, you must submit your annual return or a nil return as soon as possible.

If your scheme has ceased, you must:

enter the final event date online

submit either a return or a nil return for the ceased scheme

Taking these actions may help you avoid further penalties. You should do this even if you have already submitted, or plan to submit, an appeal against the penalty.

HMRC will not be able to respond to your appeal if you have not submitted an annual or nil return for the relevant tax year.

Read about how to deal with an employment related securities penalty.

Employer’s National Insurance contributions joint elections — reminder of the changes to the administration process

From 1 May 2025, if employers use the pre-approved National Insurance contributions election form template on gov.uk, they no longer need to submit the form to HMRC for approval.

Employers who create their own employer’s National Insurance contributions election form must still send it to HMRC for approval.

Read about transferring employer’s National Insurance to employees.

Employment related securities scheme registration process — reminder

Before you can register an employment related securities scheme, you must first be registered as an employer with HMRC. If you’re not yet registered, note that obtaining your PAYE reference number can take up to 30 working days.

Once you receive your PAYE reference, you’ll need to enrol for the PAYE online service and activate it to proceed with employment related securities registration.

Read about how to register an employment related securities scheme and what to do if you missed the deadline.

Saving copies of your end of year returns or notifications — reminder

You will not be able to access a copy of what you submit through the online service once you have submitted it.

You can view the date of your last return or notification submission by logging into your online account and navigating to the ‘View Schemes and Arrangements’ page.

Before submitting your employment related securities return or EMI notification, make sure to save a copy for your records.

If you’re entering details online, consider taking screenshots of each page, including the confirmation page.
